output.summary: MAS Financial Stability Review (22 Sep) found banks well-capitalised but ranked AI-driven cyber risk top concern; EBA finalised third-party risk guidelines; FCA opened AML probe into Euro Exchange Securities.

sources.title: AI, Cyber Emerge as Top Singapore Financials Concerns, MAS Says - Bloomberg
sources.quote: 80% of chief risk officers surveyed by MAS cited cyber and operational dangers as their top worry, compared with 77% for geopolitical risks.

sources.title: MAS Financial Stability Review 2026
sources.quote: Results of MAS top-down stress tests affirm that banks and insurers are well-capitalised and able to withstand severe macrofinancial shocks.

sources.title: Financial Regulation Weekly Bulletin - 24 September 2026
sources.quote: EBA publishes final guidelines on sound management of third-party risk related to non-ICT services (EBA/GL/2026/09), replacing 2019 outsourcing guidelines.

sources.title: EBA Finalises Guidelines on Third-Party Risk for Non-ICT Services: A More Proportionate Framework Aligned with DORA
sources.quote: The guidelines are final but awaiting translation into all EU official languages. The date of application has not yet been fixed.

sources.title: Regulatory Roundup — September 2026: AML Enforcement, Sanctions Expansion, and Heightened Crypto & AI Oversight
sources.quote: The FCA shuttered EES in June, citing 'significant risks of financial crime' after the firm reportedly moved over £2 billion for a small set of high-risk clients.
